append.text: **Ps 15:10 — the hard test this row named: *Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno* → *Porque não abandonareis a minha alma no inferno*:** kept (DRB *hell*; MS1932 here *no inferno*). The Clementine of Acts, fetched (consult/bolls-VULG-44-2.json, -44-13.json), quotes the colon word for word (Acts 2:27) and applies it to Christ in 2:31 *neque derelictus est in inferno, neque caro ejus vidit corruptionem*; 13:35 quotes 15:10b. The blind reader heard, as foreseen, **the place of punishment first, the realm of the dead second**; the Latinist passed it twice; no critic asked for a change. Options in Ps 15: *nos infernos*, *na mansão dos mortos*, *na morada dos mortos* (the Creed's wordings still unverified). With 6:6, 9:18, 17:6 the row now has its four tests — ready for Gustavo's ruling.

Ps 15:3 *mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis* → *fez maravilhosas todas as minhas vontades neles* (no subject supplied; the blind reader heard the Lord). The stylist wanted *tornou maravilhosas* — refused for this row (4:4), kept as an option.

**Ps 15:8 *Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper* → *Eu via o Senhor sempre à minha vista*** (the Latinist's line); the stylist's *diante de mim* refused for this row's noun, kept as an option. Acts 2:25 quotes it (fetched).

Ps 15:8 *a dextris est mihi* → *está à minha direita*; 15:11 *delectatiónes in déxtera tua* → *deleites na vossa direita* (in → *na*, a dextris → *à*); the blind reader heard the right hand first, the right side second.
**commovéri, Ps 15:8 *ne commóvear* → *para eu não ser abalado*** (the 118:80 build; one Greek, σαλεύω); = Acts 2:25 (fetched). Passed the Latinist twice.

append.row: | in finem | para sempre where it says perpetuity (each psalm decides) | working (D27) | Ps 12:1
append.text: **usque in finem, Ps 15:11 *delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem* → *deleites na vossa direita até o fim*** (D27 keeps usque in finem apart; affirmative, so none of 9:19's negation fault); passed the Latinist twice; the blind reader heard 'to the end of my life' first, 'of time' second. *para sempre* is the option. 37:7 *usque in finem* can follow.
Ps 15:7 *increpuérunt me renes mei* → *os meus rins me repreenderam*: the blind reader heard the organs first (a pain), conscience second — as this row foresaw; passed the Latinist twice.
Ps 15:7 *os meus rins me repreenderam* (the Greek here is ἐπαίδευσαν, 'chastened'; the Latin's 'rebuked' followed).

**Ps 15:7 and 15:9 written as this row proposed** (*e ainda até a noite os meus rins* / *e ainda a minha carne repousará*). The stylist asked for *e até a noite … também* at 15:7 ('e ainda até' piles particles; 'ainda' may be heard as duration) — refused for the pair with 15:9, kept as an option.

**Ps 15:5 *Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei* → *O Senhor é a parte da minha herança e do meu cálice*:** the proparoxytone at the mediant accepted; the stylist's *A parte … e do meu cálice é o Senhor* (the mediant on *Senhor*) refused — the verse opens on Dóminus and turns to *sois vós* — kept as an option, with *e do cálice meu*.
Ps 15:6 *Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris* → *As cordas me caíram em lugares excelentes*: the blind reader heard physical ropes first, the measuring lines of an allotment second; the image kept.
Ps 15:7 *qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum* → *que me deu entendimento*, as this row proposed; passed the Latinist twice.

**Ps 15:4b *conventícula eórum de sanguínibus* → *os seus ajuntamentos de sangue*: the plural lost as in this row, HELD against a Latinist major twice (he wants *de sangues*).** The blind reader heard 'reuniões com derramamento de sangue' first, 'ritos com sangue' second — both readings of the plural. See the new open row *sanguínes (plural)*.

egére (the verb), Ps 15:2 (DO 15:1) *quóniam bonórum meórum non eges* → *porque não precisais dos meus bens* — the plain verb; *não tendes necessidade* (MS1932, the link to *necessitado*) is the option. Only place (grep).

**conserváre, Ps 15:1 *Consérva me, Dómine* → *Conservai-me, Senhor*** — the 11:8 wording (person as object); *Guardai-me* (MS1932) refused because custodíre (16:8a *Custódi me*) needs *guardar*; passed the Latinist twice, no reader remarked. 36:28 *in ætérnum conservabúntur* can follow.

terms: | sanguínes (plural: *vir sánguinum*, *de sanguínibus*) | *sangue* (singular) | open | Ps 5:7b, 15:4b (*ajuntamentos de sangue*), 25:9, 50:16 *Líbera me de sanguínibus*, 54:24, 138:19. The Latinist (MAJOR, held twice in Ps 15) wants the plural *sangues* kept; the project has lost it since 5:7b (*homem de sangue*, DRB 'bloody'). In Portuguese *sangue* is a mass noun and *sangues* is heard as a slip; one ruling must serve all six places. **For Gustavo.** |

| conventículum | ajuntamento (*Não congregarei os seus ajuntamentos de sangue*) | open | Ps 15:4b only (grep); congregáre keeps *congregar* (one family with congregátio → congregação), so the noun is not *congregação* nor concílium's *assembleia*. MS1932 *conventículos* (apt, rare, a proparoxytone) is the option. The blind reader listed *congregarei* as unknown |

Draft 1 *antevia* (pro-vidére part for part) fell to a Latinist major, the stylist and the blind reader (unknown word; heard as 'foresaw'): the προ- is 'before me' in place, carried by *à minha vista*. Acts 2:25 quotes it; 2:31 *providens* (Peter's foresight) is Acts' reading, not the verse's |
